name: Anchored Coins AEUR
oneLiner: AEUR is Anchored Coins' centralized euro stablecoin, backed 1:1 by EUR deposits at Swissquote Bank, with the issuer winding down to comply with MiCAR.
collateral: Euro reserves held 1:1 at Swissquote Bank SA (FINMA-licensed Swiss bank)

bridgeRouteRisk.summary: AEUR is issuer-documented as available on Ethereum and BNB Chain, with no public bridge route required for holder-facing supply. The multichain posture is reviewed as issuer-native issuance/redemption exposure.

reserves.name: Euro deposits at Swissquote Bank SA

notices.title: Winding down
notices.message: FlowBank SA (former reserve partner) declared bankruptcy in June 2024. Anchored Coins has since restructured collateral so that 100% of circulating AEUR is now backed at Swissquote Bank SA; bankruptcy proceedings no longer affect coverage. The issuer is winding down stablecoin operations to comply with MiCAR (which requires EU licensing for EUR issuers) and will not resume new AEUR issuance; AEUR was delisted from Binance EEA in March 2025. Redemptions continue (minimum 250,000 AEUR threshold for direct primary-market redemption).

obituary.epitaph: A solvent euro was retired by its license boundary
obituary.obituary: Anchored Coins stopped issuing new AEUR after MiCAR made an EU issuer license necessary for the Swiss company to continue a EUR stablecoin business. The issuer moved reserves to Swissquote and kept a high-minimum redemption route for existing holders, but announced an orderly withdrawal from stablecoins rather than a relaunch. With issuance permanently closed and the product in a regulatory wind-down, Pharos freezes AEUR as an archived legacy asset while preserving its historical market record.
